videos.title: Bone Mapper Demo #2
videos.description:
Often the bones are mostly mapped by the program already, it's just a few that are missing. You only need to map the ones with "!" mark next to them and the model will work fine.
The 1.4.2 update uses circle icons to indicate the status of the bones. Empty  circle means the bone is not mapped but is not critical, meaning the model should work even without that bone being mapped. Circle with dot inside means the bone is already mapped. Circle with exclamation mark means the bone is not mapped and is critical for the model to function.

videos.title: [DanceXR] 1.4.0 New Feature: Google Drive Integration
videos.description:
Version 1.4.0 will allow you to download content from shared Google Drive folders. It checks differences between Google drive and your local folder before downloading to make sure that only new files are downloaded. 
You can use this feature to synchronize your content across multiple devices, or share to a friend.

Consider this experimental since it is not perfect. 
We are using Google Drive in a way that does not require you to login to minimize user input, but the downside of that is the Google Drive folder needs to be shared without restriction. And Google has a limit on how much you can download from the same IP address within a given period of time. If you are suddenly unable to download, that usually means you've exceeded the download limit. You'll have to wait a few hours before you can download again.

videos.title: [DanceXR] 1.4.0 Using PMX model as prop
videos.description:
In addition to the built-in models, you can also load your own PMX or XPS models as props on stage. 
To do this you need to assign the "[Props]" tag to the model, then the model will appear in the props menu and you can load it from there. 
Models loaded as prop will have additional settings including creating simple physics shapes for them. 
By default the shape is sphere, you can also choose from capsule and box shapes and change the shape size in the settings to match your model. 

In this demo the default sphere shape doesn't work with the pillow model, so we rotated the model vertically and then switched to capsule shape and updated size to match it.

videos.title: [DanceXR] 1.4.0 Built-in Props Demo
videos.description:
Demonstrating built-in props available in 1.4.0
All the primitive shapes can be configured with different textures and whether to enable physics or not. 
The screen and mirror are just the same screen feature available before. They are just separated into 2 different objects and they can now be dragged to change positions.

videos.title: [DanceXR] Softbody physics setup
videos.description:
Use the new Softbody Physics to setup dynamics for butts and thigh. It's pretty much the same with the other physics settings, you just need to select the bones and then fine tune by adjusting the spring force and other settings. 

Also in the Boobs settings you can use the "Softbody" toggle to switch between soft body mode and normal mode.

videos.title: Tag system and content selection improvements in version 1.4.0
videos.description:
Tons of long awaited features coming to 1.4.0 release. Here is a quick preview video and the short descriptions below. More details will be available soon.
* All new tag system
  1 Automatic tag creation: The program creates a list of tags derived from file and folder names for you to choose and create tags automatically. 
  2 Allows selecting multiple tags to narrow down your selection
  3 You can easily rename, merge and delete tags
  4 You can configure your tags under different categories for easier selection
* Loading external models. You can now load models outside of your content library. 
* All new playlist management: You can reorder and delete items from the playlist and save the list for later use. 
* You can now load multiple stage models. 
* Newly introduced prop models that you can place on stage. This includes a few primitive shapes and functional objects like screens and mirrors, and you can use your own models too. All you need to do is to assign a "Props" tag to your model.

videos.title: Sweet Devil x 3 - DOVXVV Koharu, Amy, Tsukushi
Configuring Music Timing With New "Tap Beats" Functionality
videos.description:
Music timing information is very important for all the procedural motions because it is used to match the motion with the music. Without it the BPM (beats per minute) is default at 120 and it won't be in sync with the music. 

In the 1.3.3 release we will include a new "tap beats" functionality for you to easily set timing information accurately. 

What you need to do is to play the music, and then tap on the button every time a beat drops. The program requires about 4 taps to calculate the average BPM and offset value for you. You can tell from the glowing ring on the floor that the light dots can match the music beats perfectly when it is set correctly. It is fine if you didn't get it right the first time, just continue tapping the beats until everything looks right. 

Previously we have a command line tool bundled with the application to parse each music file in the library and generate the timing information, that method still works but is a little hard to use and only supports WAV format and not able to read from ZIP. Video for the old method: https://youtu.be/chI-3GQS08Q

videos.title: Hair & Cloth Physics Setup Examples (Please read description below)
videos.description:
Demonstrate hair & cloth physics setup with Kasumi and Helena. 

In most cases you just need to find and select the right bones. Ponytails and ribbons are super easy. 

Sometimes there are too many child bones and to make it worse the bones you need are actually buried several levels under those child bones. In this case you can select the parent bones and then use the "Skip First X Bones" setting to fine tune your selection. 

If during the process things got messy, don't panic. Finish your selection and then you can try stablize things in the settings. First try to reduce "inter-link dist" to 0 to disable inter-link joints, then try to increase the collider size a little bit (don't overdo it), if that still doesn't work you can try disable and re-enable the settings, and then ultimately reload the model and it can sometimes resolve the instability.

videos.title: Install & load content onto Oculus Quest
videos.description:
Release 0.9 will include a demo build for Oculus Quest. This video demos how to install the build and load content onto your Quest. 

Before you start, connect your Quest to the PC, put on your Quest and selected "Allow Access" within the Quest when prompted. Otherwise you won't be able to copy content to your Quest. 

You'll need SideQuest to install the build. Follow this instructions to setup SideQuest on your Quest if you haven't done so already: https://sidequestvr.com/setup-howto

Once installed successfully, select "Unknown source" from the top-right dropdown of your app library and you'll be able to launch DVVR from there. 

On Oculus Quest you won't be able to select content folder like the desktop version does, since Android platform prevent apps from accessing files outside of their data folders. You'll have to follow exactly what's shown in the video to copy your content into.

videos.title: Motion improvements side by side comparison
videos.description:
A new feature has been added in the 0.9 release to improve motion compatibility between different models. 
Many PMX models has their center bone lower than the hips causing unwanted movements of upper body when the center is rotated. 
The new "Center Bone Offset" control offsets this unwanted movement without needing to edit your model. 
The exact same motion is being applied to both models, the one on the left has this control turned on while the one on the right has it off. You can see the difference it makes.

Here is a quick demo of the usage. The bones that are marked (!) are required while the rest are optional. In this demo I'm only mapping the required ones so that the video doesn't get too long but in reality you should try to map everybone for the best result. 

You can see that once all the required bones are mapped the models get scaled and the motion is automatically applied. You can still continue to make changes to the mappings after that.

videos.description:
DVVR 0.2.3 is released. This is mainly bug fixes & compatibility improvements. 

To get the latest build, visit our Patreon page: 
https://www.patreon.com/alloystorm

What's new:
Model compatibility
 * Ground position
 * Center Correction
 * Missing texture

Bug fixes
 * Audio motion lag
 * Actor position lock fix
 * UI fixes

New
 * Refine spotlight control
 * Simple looping
 * Micro motion
 * WASD keyboard control in VR

videos.title: DVVR Dance Viewer VR eye contact showcase 2 60fps [MMD] Conqueror
videos.description:
This is a showcase of the eye contact feature available in DVVR MMD dance viewer application we've been working on. 

Download it for free here: https://alloystorm.github.io/dvvr/

About the eye contact feature:
When you look at the dancers, they will look back and make eye contact with you until you move your eyes off them or their dance move require them to move elsewhere. You can also see that they blink their eyes naturally and there's even subtle breathing motion if you pay close attention. 

These motion are completely dynamic and not tied to the dance motion. Which means it will work in any dance motion and even when they are stopped.

videos.title: DVVR Dance Viewer VR eye contact showcase 60fps [MMD] Conqueror
videos.description:
Uploaded a second video with improved camera control: https://youtu.be/zP966sQ6h0g

This is a showcase of the eye contact feature available in DVVR MMD dance viewer application we've been working on. 

Check out the project page for more info and download when it is available soon: https://alloystorm.github.io/dvvr/

Recorded realtime at 60 fps. 

About the eye contact feature:

Pay attention to the dancer's eyes and you'll find that when being looked at, they will look back and smile back at you like a real human does. They also blink naturally. The range of motion is adjustable for each model and is not tied to the dance motion at all meaning this works for any motion and even when it is paused.
